rows.grounds: adverb of repetition, sandhi before arthaḥ
predicate noun in compound sense with repetition

items.question: Why is repeated practice unsuitable for the supreme nondual reality?
premises: Repeated practice means doing something again and again.
Such practice arises from distinctions of space and time and from connection with appearance and otherness.
The path of body, mind, breath, and senses is the domain of such distinctions.
items.inference: Therefore repeated practice belongs to the differentiated domain and cannot reach the undivided supreme reality.
items.plain_english: Practice means doing something over and over again, and even that arises from differences of space and time and from involvement with appearance and otherness; so it takes place on the path of body, mind, breath, and senses.

rows.grounds: predicate describing those who wish to enter

items.question: How do seekers become established in the Bhairava reality?
premises: The Bhairava reality is a form dense with pure light.
Some seekers wish to enter that reality.
Resting in knowledge that shines once is sufficient for establishment.
items.inference: Therefore seekers become established in the Bhairava reality through a single resting in luminous knowledge, not through repeated practice.
items.plain_english: Those who wish to enter the Bhairava form, which is dense with pure light alone, become firmly established simply by resting in knowledge that shines forth once.

rows.grounds: atra + eva + ataḥ fused in sandhi

items.question: What practice is declared supreme in this context?
premises: In this context a supreme and universally helpful limb is declared.
That limb is concentration.
Concentrations determined through that door may take on that same nature.
items.inference: Therefore concentration, when grounded in this realization, is the supreme and universally helpful practice.
items.plain_english: For that reason, concentration is declared here to be the supreme and universally helpful limb, and concentrations determined through that same door may become of that very nature.

items.question: How can confidence be placed in reasoning that lacks firm grounding?
premises: An opponent claims reasoning is ungrounded.
If reasoning is ungrounded, confidence in it seems impossible.
The same charge of groundlessness could apply to the opponent's own statement.
items.inference: The objection from groundlessness is unstable because it threatens to undermine itself.
items.plain_english: But surely, what confidence can be placed in reasoning that has no firm ground? Or else, why would your own statement not be struck down by the same lack of ground?

rows.grounds: explanatory particle, sandhi form of hi

items.question: How can scripture alone decide truth when scriptures conflict?
premises: Some hold that scripture alone is the valid means of knowledge.
There exist hosts of scriptures that contradict one another.
A contradictory set cannot by itself settle what is certain.
items.inference: Therefore scripture alone cannot serve as the final criterion when conflicting scriptures are present.
items.plain_english: Likewise, if some insist that scripture alone is the valid means of knowledge, how is certainty to be reached when there is a whole host of scriptures that contradict it?

items.question: Can majority acceptance establish scriptural validity?
premises: One might propose acceptance by the great multitude as the cause of validity.
A great multitude opposed to that position is also possible.
A criterion that can be matched by its opposite lacks firm grounding.
items.inference: Therefore majority acceptance does not securely establish validity.
items.plain_english: But if acceptance by the great multitude is taken as the reason for validity, that too is ungrounded, because a great multitude opposed to it can just as well exist.

items.question: Is ordinary perception a secure final authority?
premises: Perception in cases like taste is sometimes overruled.
Appeal to later cognitions to correct perception can continue without end.
A criterion open to endless regress is not final.
items.inference: Therefore ordinary perception is not an unquestionable final authority.
items.plain_english: Even perception, in matters like taste and so on, is seen to be overruled, and it becomes subject to an endless regress of later cognitions, does it not?

rows.grounds: subject, the expert in joining differences

items.question: How could practical life proceed if self-awareness were overruled?
premises: The opponent's critique would overrule even self-awareness.
Practical dealings depend on some trusted awareness.
A person skilled in managing differences still needs a basis for action.
items.inference: If self-awareness were overruled, coherent practical life would become impossible.
items.plain_english: If even self-awareness were overruled in that way, how could this person, skilled in joining differences together, carry on any practical dealings at all?

rows.grounds: possessive reference to the Trika position
contrastive particle, sandhi form of tu
ultimate ground of certainty; compound: bhairava-sāgara

items.question: Why does the Trika position not fall into groundlessness?
premises: The Trika position rests on the all-full supreme ocean of Bhairava.
That ocean is present everywhere.
What is grounded everywhere cannot become ungrounded at some time or place.
items.inference: Therefore the Trika position does not suffer from groundlessness.
items.plain_english: But for us there can never be groundlessness at any time or place, because for us the supreme, all-full ocean of Bhairava is present everywhere.

rows.grounds: relative pronoun introducing the qualified group

items.question: For whom does reasoning lose its charge of groundlessness?
premises: Reasoning is accused of groundlessness in general.
Some have crossed the ocean of reasoning and received the supreme nectar of awareness.
For such knowers, reasoning is no longer cut off from its ultimate ground.
items.inference: Therefore reasoning is not ungrounded for those established in the supreme nectar of awareness.
items.plain_english: Especially for those whose awareness has received the supreme nectar by crossing the ocean of reasoning, reasoning itself is not ungrounded.

items.question: Why do ordinary forms of reasoning fail to reach Śiva?
premises: All parts of reasoning can operate without touching self-awareness.
Without self-awareness, reasoning lacks its highest ground.
Śiva is the final fruit only when that ground is reached.
items.inference: Therefore reasoning that does not touch self-awareness does not attain Śiva as its final fruit.
items.plain_english: For all the parts of reasoning that do not touch self-awareness never, anywhere, attain Śiva as their final fruit.

rows.grounds: describes bheda; tatra + udbhāvitaḥ in sandhi
subject who delight in difference; compound: mūḍha-dhī

items.question: What is the true aim of scripture and where do the deluded go astray?
premises: The meaning of all scripture has non-difference as its essence.
Difference may be brought forth within scripture for the sake of attaining non-difference.
Those of deluded intellect take delight in that difference itself.
items.inference: Therefore the deluded mistake a provisional teaching of difference for scripture's final aim.
items.plain_english: The meaning of all scripture is essentially non-difference; any difference brought forth there is for attaining that non-difference, yet those of deluded intellect take delight in the difference itself.

items.question: Does reasoning have any use even within non-difference?
premises: Reasoning is skilled at cutting down arguments rooted in difference.
The ultimate teaching is non-difference.
A tool suited to difference may or may not serve non-difference.
items.inference: The question arises whether reasoning retains any usefulness in the domain of non-difference.
items.plain_english: Reasoning is skilled only in cutting down the arguments of views based on difference; but surely, does reasoning have any usefulness even in the realm of non-difference?

rows.grounds: object characterized by the relative clause

items.question: What is the supreme means to the nonduality that graces the universe?
premises: Even reasoning is not truly fitting in the vision of supreme nonduality.
Supreme nonduality is of the nature of grace to the universe.
A means suited to that reality must itself be immediate and living.
items.inference: Therefore the text declares the Heart, whose nature is vibration, as the supreme means to that nonduality.
items.plain_english: In the vision of supreme nonduality, even reasoning is not truly fitting; therefore, for that supreme nonduality whose nature is grace to the universe, the text declares the Heart, whose nature is vibration, to be the supreme means.

items.question: What is the self-reflective awareness that arises in the Heart?
premises: The Heart is made of awareness.
In it arises a self-reflective awareness that is the wonder of full consciousness.
That awareness can suddenly dissolve the outward flashing of the universe.
items.inference: The Heart's self-reflective awareness is an immediate, all-at-once absorption of universal manifestation into full consciousness.
items.plain_english: In the Heart, which is made of awareness, there is a self-reflective awareness, the wonder of full consciousness, which all at once, suddenly and forcibly, dissolves the outward flashing of the universe.

rows.grounds: demonstrative subject, sandhi form of asau

items.question: What is the universal vibration described in this teaching?
premises: There are first and last moments in the grasping of things.
In those moments a state appears that is full of surging bliss.
That bliss is identified with the bliss of the whole world.
items.inference: This state is called the universal vibration.
items.plain_english: In the first and last moments of grasping things, that state which is fully filled with surging bliss and made of the bliss of the whole world is called the universal vibration.

items.question: How does the Heart's flashing lead into the triad of powers?
premises: The Heart's flashing forth is manifest as pure being.
This flashing belongs to the abode of emission.
Recognition of that flashing corresponds to entry into the triad of powers.
items.inference: To the extent one recognizes the Heart's flashing as being, one enters the triad of powers.
items.plain_english: The manifest flashing of the Heart, which shines forth as pure being from the abode of emission, leads one into the triad of powers to the very extent that it is recognized.

items.question: How is the Heart defined and from where is it emitted?
premises: The Heart is the supreme nectar of Bhairava awareness.
It is situated on the trident of the powers of will, knowledge, and action.
From the supreme abode it is emitted outward.
items.inference: The Heart is both the nectar of Bhairava awareness and the emissive center of the three powers.
items.plain_english: This Heart is defined as the supreme nectar of Bhairava awareness, situated on the trident of the powers of will, knowledge, and action; from the supreme abode it is emitted.

items.question: How does the universe arise from the supreme Self?
premises: The universe flashes forth in the lordly supreme Self.
That universe is of the nature of consciousness.
It is situated on the trident of the three powers and proceeds by the path of emission on the Śāmbhava level.
items.inference: The universe is a conscious emission from the supreme Self through the three powers on the Śāmbhava path.
items.plain_english: In the supreme, lordly Self this universe flashes forth as consciousness, situated on the trident of the three powers, and then proceeds by the path of emission on the Śāmbhava level.

rows.grounds: iha + aham-ātmakaṃ in sandhi; compound: aham-ātmaka

items.question: What is the Heart that always shines forth?
premises: The emitted reality is proclaimed as pure being.
The Heart is full and of the nature of 'I'.
Its shining is the flashing of the union of Śiva and Śakti.
items.inference: The Heart is the ever-shining fullness of being, identical with the 'I' as the flashing union of Śiva and Śakti.
items.plain_english: That is then proclaimed as pure being; this full Heart, of the nature of 'I', always shines forth as the very flashing of the union of Śiva and Śakti.

rows.grounds: locative adverb referring to the Heart
adverb of vast multiplicity; compound: sahasra-koṭi-śas

items.question: What cosmic processes appear within the Heart?
premises: The Heart is the locus described as 'here'.
Creation, dissolution, and maintenance occur in countless sequences.
These sequences are associated with Hara, Viṣṇu, and the lotus-born creator.
items.inference: All cosmic cycles of creation, maintenance, and dissolution shine forth eternally within the Heart.
items.plain_english: Here, in the Heart, sequences of creation, dissolution, and maintenance shine forth by the hundreds or even by thousands of millions, eternally, gathered through the agencies of Hara, Viṣṇu, and the lotus-born.

items.question: How is the Heart's vibration revealed to one not ready for the prior method?
premises: Some may not be able to enter immediately through the previously stated collection of reasonings.
Such a person still needs access to the Heart's vibration.
The śākta means provides an alternative path.
items.inference: For one unable to enter by the prior reasoning, the Heart's vibration is revealed through the path of the śākta means.
items.plain_english: But for one who is not able to enter immediately through the collection of reasonings stated before, the vibration of the Heart is made manifest by the path of the śākta means.

items.question: What practice leads the practitioner into the Heart's inner path?
premises: The breath can be impelled at the tip of the trident.
That impelling opens access to the path of the Heart.
Within that path one may rest in the moon-digit of consciousness.
items.inference: By impelling the breath at the trident's tip and resting in the inner moon-digit of consciousness, the practitioner enters the Heart's path.
uncertainties: The exact yogic referent of 'tip of the trident' is technical and context-dependent.
items.plain_english: One reaches the path of the Heart by impelling the breath at the tip of the trident, and becomes intent on resting in the moon-digit of consciousness within that.

items.question: What must be abandoned to move beyond the lower states?
premises: There are states beginning with absence of bliss.
These states are situated amid the five elements.
Progress requires suddenly abandoning that level.
items.inference: By abruptly abandoning the elemental level and its joyless states, the practitioner moves beyond them.
items.plain_english: Then, suddenly, by abandoning that level and casting off those states beginning with absence of bliss, which are situated amid the five elements, one moves beyond them.
